name: Tetrahedralization Schemes
text:
# Tetrahedralization Schemes
## Overview
Tetrahedralization Schemes decompose cubic voxel cells into tetrahedra to facilitate [isosurface extraction](#30-isosurface-extraction.md), addressing topological ambiguities and artifacts inherent in standard cube-based methods like Marching Cubes [S2, unofficial]. This family focuses on the geometric partitioning strategy itself—determining vertex counts, tetrahedron shapes, and neighbor dependencies [S1, unofficial]. It sets itself apart by offering alternatives to the standard 5-tetrahedron or 6-tetrahedron decompositions, such as schemes using 12 or 24 tetrahedra, or those based on non-cubic lattices like BCC or Diamond, to improve surface smoothness or reduce lookup table memory [S1, unofficial][S2, unofficial].
## Shared principles
The core mechanism replaces the standard cubic voxel with a set of non-overlapping tetrahedra that fill the same volume [S1, unofficial]. For each tetrahedron, the scalar field values at its four vertices determine the intersection with an isosurface threshold $T$ [S2, unofficial]. The algorithm checks the sign of $(S_i - T)$ for each vertex $i$ [S1, unofficial]. If signs differ across an edge, [linear interpolation](#14935-linear-interpolation.md) finds the intersection point $P$:
$$ P = V_1 + \frac{T - S_1}{S_2 - S_1} (V_2 - V_1) $$
where $V_1, V_2$ are vertex positions and $S_1, S_2$ are scalar values [S2, unofficial]. The collection of these points forms the output triangle mesh vertices [S1, unofficial]. The specific scheme dictates tetrahedron connectivity, whether new "fabricated" points (like cell centers) are introduced, and how adjacent cells share boundaries to ensure a manifold mesh [S1, unofficial][S2, unofficial].
## Subtopics

### [BCC Marching Tetrahedra with Permutation-Based Lookup](3414-bcc-marching-tetrahedra-with-permutation-based-lookup.md)
Extracts explicit, connected triangle mesh [isosurfaces](#13788-isosurfaces.md) from Body-Centered Cubic (BCC) volume datasets on a GPU. It solves the problem of large lookup tables and complex branching in standard Marching Tetrahedra by using a single reference tetrahedron and applying 3D permutation transformations to handle all six cell types. Unlike the triangle-soup output of [classic](#5024-classic-column-voxel-space.md) MT, this method produces a manifold mesh with shared vertices, enabling efficient downstream applications such as [curvature](#11695-curvature.md) rendering. Choose this when working with BCC data and needing to minimize lookup table memory while maintaining connected mesh structures.

### [Marching Tetrahedra 3 (DLC-Plane)](3632-marching-tetrahedra-3-dlc-plane.md)
Generates isosurfaces from voxel data by decomposing the grid into a diamond crystal lattice structure composed of exactly 5 tetrahedra per cell, using only the 5 existing grid vertices without introducing fabricated points. It differs from standard Marching Cubes or other tetrahedral schemes by eliminating center-point synthesis, which prevents creases and indentations on data boundaries. The "Plane" variant specifically processes the grid plane-by-plane, generating a single calculation for all shared points to reduce total point count and memory overhead compared to the "Volume" variant. Choose this for smooth [surface extraction](#29-surface-extraction.md) when avoiding center-point artifacts is critical.

### Centered Cubic Lattice
A method that splits the cube cell into 24 tetrahedra by introducing a new data value at the center of gravity of the processed cell, computed as the arithmetic or weighted mean of the cell's vertices [S1, unofficial]. All 24 tetrahedra are identical in dimensions, similar to the MT6 method, but require interpolation on new edges among adjacent central points [S1, unofficial]. This scheme provides better detail in some aspects but has unacceptable computational time and memory requirements compared to 6-tetrahedra schemes [S2, unofficial].

### 12 Tetrahedra Scheme
A [decomposition](#7254-decomposition.md) scheme using 12 tetrahedra per voxel, based on a body-centred cubic lattice with two neighboring voxels, where all tetrahedra are identical with edge lengths $a$, $a\sqrt{3}$, $a$, $a\sqrt{3}$ if $2a$ is the voxel's edge length [S2, unofficial]. It requires considering more neighbors for iso-surface extraction than the body-centred tetrahedronal scheme [S2, unofficial].

### [Diamond Lattice Cell (DCL) Tetrahedra](16618-diamond-lattice-cell-dcl-tetrahedra.md)
Partitions cubic voxels into five tetrahedra based on a diamond cubic lattice structure. It solves the ambiguity and artifact issues of standard cube slicing by ensuring consistent diagonal interpolation across shared faces through an alternating orientation pattern. Unlike standard Marching Tetrahedra, DCL introduces additional calculations for diagonals across cube faces, making it structurally closer to Dual Contouring in its handling of face intersections. It does not address cases where two near points 'inside' a surface are a combined distance < 1 from the surface.

## Background
The need for tetrahedralization arose from the topological ambiguities in Marching Cubes, where certain configurations could produce non-manifold surfaces or artifacts [S2, unofficial]. The Centered Cubic Lattice method was compared in studies of fundamental iso-surface extraction methods [S1, unofficial]. The Diamond Lattice Cell approach is discussed in the context of alternative cube slicing and its relationship to Dual Contouring [S1, unofficial][S2, unofficial]. The BCC permutation-based lookup method addresses large lookup tables and complex branching in standard Marching Tetrahedra by using permutation transformations [S1, unofficial].
